Rule: All cells in the matrix contain the same black square, so the missing cell must also be a black square.

Each column contains the same shape type, with the bottom figure being the top figure reflected across the diagonal from bottom-left to top-right.

Each row keeps the shape in the same vertical position but moves it from the right half to the left half, turning the triangle into a square; in the second row, the upper-right triangle becomes an upper-left square.
In each row, the circle becomes a square while preserving the left-white/right-black vertical split.
Each column contains the same shape reflected across the horizontal axis, so the missing cell is a square in the upper-left position.
Each row changes the outer shape from circle to square while keeping the right half black; each column keeps the shape and shading, so the missing cell is a square with its right half black.
The shape changes from circle to square in each row while keeping the same left-white/right-black split, and the circle is unchanged down the column.
In each row, the shape changes from a circle to a square while the black-right shading remains the same, so the missing cell is a square with the right half black.

Across each row, the shape changes from a circle to a square while the left-white/right-black shading stays the same; down each column, both shape and shading remain the same, so the missing cell is a square with the left half white and right half black.
The shape changes from circle to square across each row while keeping the same vertical left-white/right-black fill pattern, and down each column the shape and fill pattern remain identical.
Each row contains the same number of concentric squares, increasing by one from top to bottom, so the missing cell must have three nested squares.
The outer square increases in size by a constant amount across each row and down each column, while the central black square remains fixed.
Each row contains a constant number of concentric squares equal to the row number; the missing cell must contain three nested squares, matching the other third-row cells.
Each row contains the same number of nested squares, and the third row has three nested squares.
Each row has the same number of nested squares and each column adds one outer square, so the missing cell must be the same three nested squares as in G and H.
Each row contains the same number of concentric squares, increasing from one in the top row to three in the bottom row, so the missing cell must have three nested squares like G and H.

The outer square grows larger across each row and down each column, while each figure is a square outline containing a filled black square, so the missing cell must be the largest square with a filled black square.
In each row and column, identical black squares turn white while blank/black combinations become black, so the missing cell has four white outlined squares.
The outer square increases in size across each row and column, while the central black square remains the same size.
Each row contains identical figures, with the number of concentric squares increasing by one per row; the missing cell must have three nested squares matching G and H.
The outer square grows larger by one step moving right and down, while the centered black square is always present, so the missing figure is the next larger square with a black center.
The number of nested squares increases by one in each row and each column, so the missing cell must contain three nested squares matching those in G and H.
Each row and column increases the number of nested squares by one, so the missing cell must contain three nested squares.
Each row and column adds one concentric square, so the missing cell must have three nested squares matching the third row.
Each row contains the same number of nested squares, and each column adds one outer square as you go down, so the missing cell must have three nested squares matching G and H.

Across each row, the outer shape changes from circle to diamond to square while the inner black shape stays constant; down each column, the inner shape changes from plus to star to heart while the outer shape stays constant.

In each row, the first cell shows a shape inside a circle, the second cell is that shape with a white circular hole, and the third cell is that shape with dots above and below; the shape changes from square to diamond to octagon down the rows.
Each column adds one concentric square to the figure, so the missing cell in row 3 must contain three nested squares identical to cells G and H.
Each row contains the same number of nested squares, and each column adds one nested square; the missing cell should have three nested squares matching G and H.
The outer square increases in size across rows and down columns while the inner black square remains constant.
In each row and column, the outer square grows larger while the inner black square stays the same size, so the missing cell is the largest square with a centered black square.
The number of nested squares increases by one from row to row (1, 2, 3), so the missing cell must contain three concentric squares.
Each row repeats the same figure while the number of nested squares increases by one down each row/column, so the missing cell must contain three nested squares.
The outer square increases in size across rows and columns while the central black square remains constant; the missing cell is the large square containing the black square.
The outer square increases in size across each row and down each column, while the inner black square stays the same size.
The number of nested squares increases by one moving down each column, so the missing cell must contain three nested squares.
In each row, the third cell is the union (superposition) of the first two cells.
The number of concentric squares increases by one from row to row, so the missing cell must contain three concentric squares.
The third figure in each row/column is the first figure with the second figure subtracted (overlapping parts are removed, and the small square erases the star's center).

Each row has the same number of nested squares, and the number of squares increases by one in each successive row, so the missing cell must contain three nested squares like the other third-row cells.
Each row repeats the same figure, and moving down adds one nested square, so the missing cell is the same three nested squares as in cell H.
In each row, the third figure is the symmetric difference (XOR) of the first two figures: lines that appear in both cancel out, and the remaining lines are combined.
In each row and column, the third cell is made from the top shape of the first cell and the bottom shape of the second cell.
The third cell in each row is the intersection (overlapping area) of the first two mirror-image shapes.
Each row's third cell is the pixel-wise intersection of the first two cells, so the missing cell is the overlap of G and H.
Combine the first two cells in each row or column and cancel one up-pointing triangle against one down-pointing triangle, leaving the remainder in the last cell.

In each row, the first figure is a triangle on the right half and the second is a square on the left half at the same vertical level; in each column, the shapes move upward while staying on the same side. The missing cell is therefore an upper-left square.
Each column flips the top figure vertically across the horizontal axis; applying this to the top-right square gives a square in the lower-left.
Each figure in the top row is reflected vertically to form the corresponding figure in the bottom row.

Each row and column keeps the same vertical fill pattern (left white, right black) while the shape alternates between circle and square; the missing cell should be a square with the left half white and right half black.
Each row keeps the same vertical split (left white, right black) but changes from a circle to a square, so the missing cell is a square with the right half black.
Each figure rotates 90° counterclockwise and changes from solid black to diagonal stripes across rows, while columns rotate 180° with fill unchanged.
Each row has the same left-white/right-black split, while the shape changes from circle in the first column to square in the second column.
In each row, the shape changes from a circle to a square while keeping the same left-white/right-black split; the missing cell should be a square with that same split.
The shape changes from circle to square while keeping the right half black, so the missing cell is a square with the right half black.
The shape changes from circle to square across each row while keeping the same vertical fill pattern (left white, right black).

Each row keeps the same left-right shading (white left, black right) while the shape changes from circle in the first column to square in the second column; the missing cell should be a square with white left and black right.
Each row shows the same half-filled pattern applied to a circle in the first column and a square in the second column, so the missing cell is a square with left white and right black.
The figure with a filled black center moves diagonally down the matrix, so the missing cell must match cells A and E.
The number of small squares increases by one across each row and down each column, so the missing cell should contain five horizontal squares.
The number of concentric squares increases by one across each row and down each column, so the missing cell must contain three nested squares matching the third row.
The number of vertical lines is constant per row (1, 2, 3) while the number of horizontal lines increases by 1 across each row, so the missing cell has 3 vertical and 3 horizontal lines.
In each row and column, the number of shapes decreases by one and the shape alternates between circles and squares, so the missing cell has zero shapes.

Each row and column contains one shape type (triangle, circle, square), the number of shapes increases by 1, 2, and 3 across rows respectively, and fill alternates open-filled-open, so the missing cell must contain 9 open squares.
Each row increases the number of triangles by 1, 2, 3 while alternating orientation; the missing cell has 9 downward triangles.
Across each row and down each column, the texture progresses from solid black to diagonal stripes to dot grid, so the missing cell must be entirely dot grid.
The number of nested squares increases by one each row, so the missing cell must contain three nested squares like the other cells in the third row.
The number of concentric squares increases by one in each row and column, so the missing cell must contain three nested squares.
Each row increases the number of items, and each column has a consistent shape: triangles, circles, then squares, so the missing cell should have 9 squares.
Each row and column contains one triangle, circle, and square, and one small, medium, and large size; the missing cell must be a medium circle.
Moving right adds the top-right quadrant; moving down adds the bottom-left quadrant. Applying this to the left-half shape gives the square that is black except for the bottom-right quadrant.
Each shape rotates 90 degrees clockwise across each row and down each column, so the missing cell must have a notch opening to the right.
Across each row and column, the outer square increases in size while the central black square stays the same size.
The right-angle vertex of the triangle advances one position clockwise around the square across rows and down columns, so the missing cell is the downward-pointing triangle.
In each row, the third cell is the horizontal mirror image of the first cell.
Each row keeps the outer border style constant while the inner symbol cycles through star, flower, and diamond; the missing cell must have a double border and flower.
Each row and column contains each shape (star, heart, octagon) and each fill pattern (outline, striped, solid) exactly once, so the missing cell is a striped star.

Each row and column contains exactly one single, one side-by-side pair, and one triangular formation, with counts 1, 2, 3, two hollow shapes, and one right-pointing shape; the missing cell must be two hollow right-pointing triangles side by side.
Each row and column contains each orientation (vertical, horizontal, cross) and each background pattern (white, checker, stripes) exactly once; the missing cell must be a white cross.

The third column consists of the three small triangles from column 2 rotated to match the orientation of the large filled triangle in column 1, so the missing cell has three downward triangles arranged as a 180-degree rotation of column 2.

Each row and column contains exactly one figure with a curved line, and the total number of line segments in each column is 9 (with row totals increasing 8, 9, 10), so the missing cell must be a curved 4-segment shape.
Each row and column contains one set of closed shapes, one set of lines, and one set of crosses, with element counts 2, 3, and 4 in some order; the missing cell needs 2 curved lines.
Each cell is the symmetric difference (XOR) of the two other cells in its row and column; the missing cell is the XOR of G and H, a bottom-row horizontal rectangle.
In every row and column, the third panel is the union/superposition of the first two panels: a triangle is black if it appears black in either of the first two panels.
The third figure in each row and column is the intersection (common shapes) of the first two figures.

In each row, the first figure is formed by placing the second figure on the left and the third figure on the right; therefore the missing figure is the vertical-striped rectangle that completes G when placed to the right of H.
Each row and column increases the polygon's number of sides by 2, so the missing cell must be a 12-sided polygon.
Across each row the total number of figures increases from 4 to 5 to 6, and the third column always contains exactly two figures, so the missing cell must contain two figures.
The number of star points increases by 2 across each row and down each column, so the missing cell must contain a 12-pointed star.
In each row, the third shape's number of sides/points is the absolute difference between the first two shapes' numbers, so row 3 gives |4-12|=8, an 8-pointed star.
In each row, the first figure rotated 90° clockwise gives the third figure, so the left-facing first figure in row 3 becomes an upward-facing circle.
In each row and column, assign up=+1 and down=-1, add the first two cells' values; the third cell has that many triangles, all pointed in the direction of the sign. Thus ? = +1 (one up triangle).

Starting from one circle in the center, each step adds one new shape in a new grid position, alternating the added shape type between X and O; the missing cell is the final 9-shape grid with the added shape being an O.
The number of birds on the perch increases by 1 across each row and down each column, so the missing cell needs 5 birds.
